hints: Notice this is a two-step route, so think about which alkene could sit in the middle between the alcohol and the chloroalkane.
Reagent M must remove water from propan-2-ol to form propene, which needs a concentrated acid dehydrating agent.
Once propene is formed, consider which reagent adds H and Cl across the double bond to place Cl on the middle carbon.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two-step strategy**

Great start. Going straight from an alcohol to a chloroalkane is normally one step, so two reagents tells us we go via an alkene.

We need: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ to alkene to $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_3$.

**Dehydrate with reagent M**

Alcohols lose water to form alkenes when heated with a concentrated acid dehydrating agent. Here propan-2-ol loses $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to give propene.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Concentrated $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ is the standard clean dehydrating agent for this.

**Add HCl with reagent N**

Now we do electrophilic addition to the double bond. $\text{HCl}$ adds H to one carbon and Cl to the other.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_3$$
By Markovnikov addition, H adds to the end carbon and Cl adds to the middle carbon, giving exactly 2-chloropropane.

options.A: Incorrect. Concentrated NaOH cannot dehydrate an alcohol to an alkene, it has no dehydrating action. Also $Cl_2$ adds across a double bond to give a dichloro compound, $CH_3CHClCH_2Cl$, not a monochloro compound.
options.B: Incorrect. Concentrated $H_2SO_4$ can dehydrate to propene, but reagent N is wrong. $Cl_2$ undergoes electrophilic addition to give 1,2-dichloropropane, not 2-chloropropane. We need HCl to add only one Cl.
options.C: Correct. Concentrated $H_3PO_4$ dehydrates propan-2-ol to propene, then HCl adds by Markovnikov addition to give 2-chloropropane on the secondary carbon. This is the clean two-step route.
options.D: Incorrect. Although HCl is the correct second reagent, concentrated NaOH as reagent M will not convert the alcohol to propene. A base does not eliminate water in this way, so the route never starts.
